    4

    The plan formula: going to

    No grammar rules. Just say it!★ core

    ✅ Plan

    I’m going to pack tonight.

    We’re going to book a table.

    ❌ No plan

    I’m not going to work on Sunday.

    She’s not going to come.

    ❓ Question

    Are you going to play tonight?

    Yes, I am. / No, I’m not.

    🇺🇸 Say it like an American: going to → gonna   “I’m gonna pack tonight.” “Are you gonna play?”

    Say gonna in speaking. Write going to in emails and messages to clients.

    My week planner Teacher asks: “What are you going to do on Friday?” You: “I’m going to …”

    Making suggestions

    Suggest something. Answer like a native.★ core

    💡 Suggest

    How about + place / time? How about nine?

    How about + -ing? How about ordering pizza?

    Why don’t we …? Why don’t we go bowling?

    Let’s … Let’s play one more game!

    💬 Answer

    Sounds good! / Perfect! / Sure, why not?

    I don’t mind. You choose.

    Hmm, that’s a bit early / late.

    Sorry, I can’t. I’m busy. How about …?

    A  Listen. Two people make a plan.
    🎧 Making a plan
    In the main square, under the big clock · Six · It’s quite early · Seven thirty
    B  Build the chat. Tap the messages in the right order.
    C  Answer with a suggestion: How about …? / Why don’t we …? / Let’s …
